summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and multiple airway reconstructions was admitted for increased trach site pain, chest discomfort, and reduced oral intake due to pain. She was initially managed with NPO status and IV pain control. ENT evaluation and CT trachea showed no infection, inflammation, or structural cause for pain. She resumed her prior diet after speech and swallow assessment confirmed safety. Pain was transitioned from IV morphine to oral oxycodone, with plans to continue home medications. Lightheadedness resolved with IV fluids and improved intake. Chronic microcytic anemia was noted and recommended for outpatient workup. A stable 7 mm liver hypodensity was identified on CT and communicated to her PCP. She improved clinically and was discharged home with instructions to monitor for worsening symptoms and complete follow-up for anemia and liver imaging.
problems: Other anomalies of larynx, trachea, and bronchus
